en: The Apadāna of the Elder Tālaphaladāyaka Kaṇikāra Chapter 9 I was a merchant in the city of Benares, and I gave a palm fruit to the Buddha Vipassī. Because of that deed, I have been reborn for ninety-one aeons in the heavens of the gods. For eighty-four thousand aeons I lived as a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a lord of the four continents, possessing the seven treasures. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in the city of Sāvatthī; there I was born into a wealthy family. When I had grown up, I went forth into homelessness under the Teacher Gotama. Having attained arahantship, I now dwell in peace. By means of this gift of a palm fruit, I have reached the state of coolness (nibbāna). This is my true lineage; this is my true heritage. My birth is exhausted; there will be no further existence.
“The Blessed One named Sataraṃsī, the self-become, the unconquered, having emerged from seclusion, Please provide the text you would like me to translate.
I am ready to assist you with your request. Please provide the text.
He went forth to seek alms.
Seeing him with fruit in hand,
I approached that bull among men.
With a clear mind and joyful heart,
I gave a palm fruit.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
Whatever fruit I gave back then,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of giving fruit.
The defilements have been burnt away by me; ... [as before] ...
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Tālaphaladāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the ninth legend of the elder Tālaphaladāyaka.
